# DiscordBridgeAPI

A PowerNukkitX (PNX) plugin that connects your Minecraft server to a Discord bot, and exposes a clean API so other plugins can send messages, receive Discord events, and manage bot presence — without ever touching JDA directly.

---

## Work in Progress

Currently developing new features to extend the bridge’s capabilities:

- **Automatic role assignment** – Give Discord roles based on in‑game permissions, ranks, or events.
- **Discord ↔ Minecraft account linking** – Link a player’s Discord ID to their Minecraft UUID, enabling cross‑platform features like verified roles, stats display, and more.

These features are not yet implemented, but they are planned for future releases. Stay tuned!

---

## How It Works

DiscordBridgeAPI has three modules:

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `api` | Interfaces and data classes your plugin compiles against |
| `plugin` | The server plugin that connects to Discord (drop into `/plugins/`) |

Your plugin only ever depends on the `api` jar. The `plugin` jar (which bundles JDA) lives on the server and provides the real implementation at runtime.

---

## Setup

### 1. Create a Discord bot

1. Go to [discord.com/developers/applications](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and create a new application.
2. Under **Bot**, enable the **Message Content Intent** (required to read message text).
3. Copy the bot token.
4. Invite the bot to your server with at minimum the `Send Messages` and `Read Message History` permissions.

### 2. Configure the plugin

Drop `DiscordBridgeAPI-plugin-1.0.0.jar` into your server's `/plugins/` folder, then start (or restart) the server. A `config.yml` is generated automatically:

```yaml
# plugins/DiscordBridgeAPI/config.yml
bot-token: "REPLACE_ME"
```

Replace `REPLACE_ME` with your bot token and restart the server. You should see a log line like:

```
[DiscordBridgeAPI] Connected to Discord as YourBot#1234
```

---

## Using the API in Your Plugin

### 1. Add the dependency

Add the API jar as a `provided` dependency in your `pom.xml`. It must **not** be bundled in your plugin jar — the server supplies the implementation at runtime.

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.discord</groupId>
    <artifactId>DiscordBridgeAPI-api</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
    <scope>provided</scope>
</dependency>
```

### 2. Declare the dependency in plugin.yml

This ensures PNX loads DiscordBridgeAPI before your plugin:

```yaml
name: MyPlugin
version: "1.0.0"
api: ["3.0.0"]
main: com.example.myplugin.MyPlugin
depend:
  - DiscordBridgeAPI
```

### 3. Obtain the API

There are two safe ways to get a `DiscordBotAPI` reference.

**Option A — Service manager (simple, works when load order is guaranteed):**

```java
RegisteredServiceProvider<DiscordBotAPI> rsp =
    Server.getInstance().getServiceManager().getProvider(DiscordBotAPI.class);

if (rsp != null) {
    DiscordBotAPI api = rsp.getProvider();
}
```

**Option B — `BotReadyEvent` (recommended, works even if the bot connects after your plugin enables):**

```java
@EventHandler
public void onBotReady(BotReadyEvent event) {
    DiscordBotAPI api = event.getAPI();
    // safe to use immediately
}
```

### 4. Send messages

```java
// Fire-and-forget
api.sendMessage("123456789012345678", "Hello from Minecraft!");

// Async with result
api.sendMessageAsync("123456789012345678", "Hello!")
   .thenAccept(msg -> getLogger().info("Sent: " + msg.getId()))
   .exceptionally(err -> { getLogger().error("Failed", err); return null; });
```

### 5. Send embeds

```java
EmbedData embed = EmbedData.builder()
    .title("Server Alert")
    .description("The server will restart in 5 minutes.")
    .color(Color.ORANGE)
    .footer("PowerNukkitX")
    .field("Players online", String.valueOf(Server.getInstance().getOnlinePlayers().size()), true)
    .build();

api.sendEmbed("123456789012345678", embed);
```

### 6. Listen for Discord messages

**Method A — Lambda handler (per-channel, runs on JDA thread):**

```java
api.registerMessageHandler("987654321098765432", ctx -> {
    // Marshal to server thread before touching game state
    String text = "§9[Discord] §f" + ctx.getAuthorName() + "§7: " + ctx.getContent();
    Server.getInstance().getScheduler().scheduleTask(myPlugin,
            () -> Server.getInstance().broadcastMessage(text));
}, this);
```

**Method B — PNX `@EventHandler` (fires on the server thread automatically):**

```java
@EventHandler
public void onDiscordMessage(DiscordMessageEvent event) {
    if (!event.getChannelId().equals("987654321098765432")) return;

    Server.getInstance().broadcastMessage(
        "§9[Discord] §f" + event.getAuthorName() + "§7: " + event.getContent());
}
```

> Handlers registered with `registerMessageHandler` are cleaned up automatically when your plugin disables. You can also call `api.unregisterHandlers(this)` early if needed.

### 7. Manage bot presence

```java
// Set a "Playing ..." activity
api.setActivity("on " + Server.getInstance().getMotd());

// Clear it
api.setActivity(null);

// Set status: "online", "idle", "dnd", or "invisible"
api.setStatus("idle");
```

---

## API Reference

### `DiscordBotAPI`

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `getJDA()` | Returns the underlying JDA instance |
| `isReady()` | Returns `true` if the bot is connected |
| `sendMessage(channelId, text)` | Sends a plain-text message (silent failure) |
| `sendMessageAsync(channelId, text)` | Sends a message, returns a `CompletableFuture` |
| `sendEmbed(channelId, embed)` | Sends a rich embed |
| `getChannel(channelId)` | Returns a `TextChannel` by ID, or `null` |
| `getGuilds()` | Returns all guilds the bot is in |
| `registerMessageHandler(channelId, handler, plugin)` | Registers a per-channel message callback |
| `unregisterHandlers(plugin)` | Removes all handlers owned by the plugin |
| `setActivity(text)` | Sets the bot's "Playing …" status (`null` to clear) |
| `setStatus(status)` | Sets online status: `online`, `idle`, `dnd`, `invisible` |

### `EmbedData` builder methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `.title(text)` | Embed title |
| `.description(text)` | Main body text |
| `.url(url)` | Makes the title a hyperlink |
| `.color(color)` | Left-border colour (`java.awt.Color`) |
| `.thumbnail(url)` | Small image in the top-right |
| `.image(url)` | Large image at the bottom |
| `.author(name)` / `.author(name, iconUrl)` | Author line at the top |
| `.footer(text)` / `.footer(text, iconUrl)` | Footer line at the bottom |
| `.field(name, value)` | Adds a block field |
| `.field(name, value, inline)` | Adds an inline field |

### Events

| Event | Thread | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `BotReadyEvent` | Server thread | Fired once the bot is fully connected and the service is registered |
| `DiscordMessageEvent` | Server thread | Fired for every incoming Discord message in a watched channel |

---

## Building from Source

Requires Java 21 and Maven.

```bash
git clone <repo-url>
cd DiscordBridgeAPI
mvn clean package
```
